description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review), Pass 4 of the ignored-tests audit (#993)
-- the first read of the companion suite's count-blessed t/op rows.
PRE-EXISTING.

REPRO (scratch/p49-stat-bareword.pl) -- note the handle is OPEN and VALID:

    open(FH, '<', '/etc/passwd') or die "open: $!";
    my @a = stat(FH);
    print scalar(@a), "\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  13
  PCL:          Unhandled unbound-variable: The variable FH is unbound.
                (the whole program dies at that form)

The lexical spelling is correct in both: `open(my $fh,...); stat($fh)` gives 13
under PCL too (scratch/p50-stat-errno-only.pl), and so does `stat("path")`.
So the emission is fine everywhere except the BAREWORD handle in this
argument slot, where the name is emitted as a bare CL symbol instead of being
resolved as a filehandle.

THIS IS #452's PREDICATE FAMILY.  #452 widened `_bareword_fh_p` because it
tested a PLAIN identifier and so missed `main::FH`, which made `<main::FH2>`
emit a bare CL symbol -- dead at LOAD, whole file lost.  This is the same
failure mode at a slot that predicate does not reach: `stat`/`lstat`/`-X`.
Fix it the same way -- one predicate, every slot -- and grep for the other
argument positions in the same pass (CLAUDE.md rule 11: count the parse paths).

WHAT IT COSTS, MEASURED (s464ay t/op run, .suitelog-s464ay):
  * t/op/stat_errors.t -- 333 failing rows, the 4th largest cluster in t/op
    and previously UNEXPLAINED.  The file is built entirely out of
    `stat NEVEROPENED` / `-X NEVEROPENED` bareword-handle forms.
  * t/op/write.t -- the runner's abort note is `The variable OUT is unbound`
    x21, and 477 of that file's 500 rows are the contiguous MISSING tail after
    it.  `format`/`write` is separately not-supported, but the file dies on
    THIS before it gets there.
Both files' rows are blessed inside their per-file COUNT in
baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv, which is why an ~810-row crash has no owner.

SEPARATE, SAME FILE: #1033 -- filetests do not set `$!` on failure, and a
closed handle reports ENOENT where perl reports EBADF.  That one is the
VALUE half of stat_errors.t and needs this crash fixed before its rows can be
counted.

=== DONE (s465ba, Opus, round 23) ===

RUNTIME ONLY.  No `Pl/` file changed, so the emission is unchanged BY
CONSTRUCTION -- no generation bump, no artifact regeneration, corpus-diff and
emission-ab cannot move and were not run (the WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN `cl/**` row:
gate + FULL sweep + the companion dirs the change touches + a rule-12 read of
the touched dispatch).

WHY THE RUNTIME AND NOT THE COMPILER.  The task pointed at #452's compiler-side
predicate (`_bareword_fh_p` + `_fh_sym`, which quote for `readline` and the
print `:fh` slot).  But the CONTRACT the handle builtins actually run on is
the other one: `p-open`, `p-close`, `p-eof`, `p-tell`, `p-seek`, `p-binmode`,
`p-fileno`, `p-readline` -- and `p--t`, which IS a filetest and whose docstring
already says "bareword filehandle is auto-quoted (like p-fileno)" -- take the
bare symbol from codegen and quote it in a runtime MACRO, `%p-fh-arg`.
`%p-stat-arg`, the single funnel both `stat` and `%p--path` already go through,
has ALWAYS accepted a symbol naming a handle.  So the family had a sibling and
a funnel; the only thing missing was the quote at the call site (rule 11).

THE FIX: `p-stat`, `p-lstat` and the 26 filetests become macros over
`%`â¦`-impl` bodies, exactly as `p--t`/`%p--t-impl` already were.  One
generator, `%define-fh-slot-op`, and 28 one-line registrations, so the list is
greppable and the shape cannot drift.  `p--R`/`p--W`/`p--X` call their siblings
directly (`%p--r-impl` etc.) -- routing THOSE through the macro would have
quoted their `file` PARAMETER as a handle name.

TWO EXCLUSIONS, both load-bearing, both probed:
  * `_` is the runtime's stat-cache VARIABLE (`defvar _ '%pcl-stat-cache`),
    which `-f _` READS.  Quoting it would look up a handle named "_".  The
    exclusion is in `%p-fh-arg` itself, where the question "is this bare symbol
    a handle NAME" lives.
  * The `(pl-NAME)` arm is switched OFF for this family, via a new optional
    `call-form-is-a-handle` parameter.  In a READ slot perl CALLS a declared
    sub -- `sub SPATH {"/etc/passwd"} -e SPATH` is TRUE and `use constant
    CPATH => â¦; -e CPATH` reads the constant (probed 5.40.3) -- and the
    filetest emitter ALREADY gets that right, emitting `(p--e (pl-SPATH))`.
    Turning that call back into a handle name would have been a NEW silent
    wrong.  `open` keeps the arm ON: its first argument is a GLOB slot, not a
    read slot.

MEASURED.
  * scratch/p10-stat-bareword.pl: 12 rows, was "The variable FH is unbound"
    (whole program dead), now byte-identical to perl.
  * scratch/p11-perl-bareword-slot.pl: 12 rows, 10 now identical to perl.
    The two that are not are separate PRE-EXISTING bugs, filed: #1043
    (`stat` in SCALAR context answers the 13-element list, not perl's 1) and
    #1044 (a bareword ARGUMENT that names a declared sub is read as a handle
    name -- the residue, see below).
  * GATE: <FILL>.  FULL SWEEP: <FILL>.  COMPANION io/ + op/: <FILL>.

THE RESIDUE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED -> #1044.  `stat(CONSTANT)` /
`stat(DECLARED_SUB)` now answer 0 (the handle-name reading) where they used to
CRASH; that is the same answer `eof(CONSTANT)` and `close(CONSTANT)` have
always given, i.e. a pre-existing family divergence rather than a new shape.
Its POPULATION is zero: scratch/scan-stat-bareword.pl over perl-tests/, lib/,
Pl/t/, cpan-tests/, examples/ AND perl's own t/ -- 1452 files, 2412 bareword
operand slots -- finds the colliding shape 0 times (all 33 raw hits are `_`,
which is excluded, or a bareword inside a test DESCRIPTION string).

GUARD: Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t, 54 rows in 1.4 s (27 assertions x both
emission paths).  Every expectation is the OUTPUT OF THE SAME PROGRAM under
perl 5.40.3 (scratch/guard-fh-prog.pl), and 8 of the 27 rows exist to hold the
things that must NOT move: the `_` cache (13-16), the constant/sub call
(21-23), the lexical and path spellings (19-20).  INVERSE-VERIFIED on a
1fed80b worktree: 54 of 54 FAIL -- the program dies at the first `stat(FH)`
and produces no rows at all, which is the bug itself.

ALSO FILED from the probes, both PRE-EXISTING and both verified on a 1fed80b
worktree: #1042 (`$^T` is frozen into the SAVED CORE, so `-M`/`-A`/`-C` answer
a negative age that grows with the core's age -- 184 s on one tree, 2831 s on
an older one, 0 in perl) and #1043 above.

=== s469bf (2026-09-05, Opus) — a THIRD companion file this change moved, found and
=== bisected while attributing s468's ROW DIFF for re/ comp/ run/ ===

  run/fresh_perl.t  57/34 XDIFF  ->  59/32   (perl 91/0)

Two of its 34 registered diverging rows stopped diverging, which made the file
read STALE and FAIL every run since round 23 landed.  Both rows are this task's
two named builtins:

  open(H,'run/fresh_perl.t'); # must be in the 't' d...   the bareword handle in
      `open` — and the file's snapshot `sig` column literally read `unbound:H`,
      which is the bare CL symbol this change removed;
  \# 20001210.003 (\#4893) mjd@plover.com                 t/run/fresh_perl.t:572-586,
      whose body is `format REMITOUT = … for $lineno (1..61) { write REMITOUT }` —
      the `p-write` half the audit of all 44 handle-taking builtins turned up.

BISECTED, not deduced: a `1fed80b` worktree reads 57/34 XDIFF with `unbound:H`;
a `0e7c5e3` worktree (after BA's #1028 + #1032) reads 59/32 STALE naming the same
two rows; main `c80b1a0` is identical to `0e7c5e3`.

WHY IT REACHED MAIN UNCOUNTED, and it is the reusable lesson: BA's companion leg
was `--dir io --dir op`, so run/ was never opened — and s468be's ROW DIFF
attribution could not have seen it either, because run/fresh_perl.t is
XDIFF-registered and an XDIFF file's rows are gated by the #185
`perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv` registry, NOT by I1's ROW DIFF (`row_gated_here`
excludes them so one row has exactly one gate).  A file whose registered rows
START PASSING therefore shows up as a STALE *status*, in the per-file lines, and
nowhere in the NEW/FIXED buckets a reader scans.  When a change fixes a class of
crash, the STALE column is where its uncounted wins are.

s469bf re-blessed the two rows out of `baselines/perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv`
(`--bless-rows` on that file alone, 2564 -> 2562 rows, no other row touched) and
spliced the snapshot row with the bisection in its annotation.
subject: CRASH (kills two whole companion files, ~810 rows): a BAREWORD filehandle in a `stat`/`lstat`/filetest argument slot is emitted as a bare CL symbol -- "The variable FH is unbound" -- even for an OPENED handle; the lexical `stat($fh)` spelling is correct.  Same predicate family as #452.
